timing_authorization: The implementer asked the user to stop other applications before the measurement, and the user answered to go on; asked after the run, the user answered that the other applications were stopped during it (2026-11-22).
method: time.fs in two fresh processes of the release build. Each case: 20 frames to warm up, then 5 runs of 200 frames, with WINDOW-SMOOTH off, on, off, on (20 runs of each a case over the two processes). A frame changes one pixel, calls SHOW, and waits with WINDOW-PAINT-WAIT until the window has drawn it; UTIME around the 200 frames, divided by 200: each value is the mean of 200 frames, and no single frame was timed. The time is of the whole loop: setting the pixel, SHOW (the copy of the image), the scaling, GDI drawing the image, and the wait; not of the scaling alone. WINDOW-PAINT-WAIT returns when the window has given the whole image to GDI, which is before it paints the margin and ends the paint.
notes: By a whole factor the window draws by the nearest-neighbour path also with WINDOW-SMOOTH on, so the two are equal.
A build without optimization (zig build) gave about 4.8, 9.7, 16.2 and 22.4 ms a frame with WINDOW-SMOOTH on in the four other cases, in one run before these.
Not measured: other displays and scales, fullscreen, larger images, other machines.
